title: Test Assertions
concept: Assertion macros verify expected outcomes and produce clear failure messages
why: A test without an assertion is a wish. Assertions are the verification step that turns a test from 'I hope this works' to 'I know this works.' XIOM provides specialized assertion macros that produce detailed failure messages showing expected vs actual values, making debugging failing tests fast.
theory: XIOM's test assertions: `assert_eq(a, b)` — values must be equal (requires `Eq` trait); `assert_ne(a, b)` — values must differ; `assert(condition)` — bool must be true; `assert_approx(a, b, epsilon)` — floating point within tolerance; `assert_ok(result)` — Result must be Ok; `assert_err(result)` — Result must be Err. Failed assertions panic with a message including file, line number, and a diff of expected vs actual. The `Debug` trait must be implemented for values in assertion macros.
syntax_ref:
assert_eq(<actual>, <expected>)
assert_ne(<left>, <right>)
assert(<boolean expression>)
assert_approx(<actual>, <expected>, <epsilon>)
assert_ok(<Result value>)
assert_err(<Result value>)
tips: Always put expected value second in `assert_eq(actual, expected)`
Use `assert_approx` for floating-point — never `assert_eq` on floats
common_mistakes: Swapping expected and actual — most runners display them differently
Forgetting to derive `Debug` and `Eq` on custom types used in assertions
